title: jpack.json project configuration
description: A NON-NORMATIVE convention of the judgment-pack runtime (ADR-0012), not part of the Judgment Pack Specification. It names the packs a project owns and where they live, relative to this file's own directory — under configVersion "2" the experimental graphs composing them (ADR-0017), under "3" the directory this project asks its evaluations to be recorded in (ADR-0018), under "4" whether its deciding runs must apply its reviewed set (ADR-0044), under "5" whether its evaluations must refuse a fact no comparison that reads it can match (ADR-0046), and under "6" whether that record is chained (ADR-0047). It selects nothing at decision time, templates nothing, and holds no pack's version as a truth of its own: a pack's identity is the pack document's, and every reference to it here is validated against that document rather than believed.

allOf.description: The version gate: graphs are the "2" shape's one addition, so a configuration declaring them under "1" is told exactly which member to change rather than handed an unknown-member refusal. "3", "4", "5" and "6" read them too — a later shape adds a member, it does not drop one.
The same gate for audit, the "3" shape's one addition: a configuration asking for an audit trail under an earlier version is told exactly which member to change. "4", "5" and "6" read it too.
The same gate for requireReviewed, the "4" shape's one addition. "5" and "6" read it too.
The same gate for requireComparableFacts, the "5" shape's one addition. "6" reads it too.
The same gate for the audit member's chain, the "6" shape's one addition: a configuration saying whether its trail is chained under an earlier version is told exactly which member to change.

audit.description: The directory this project's evaluation records are appended to (ADR-0018), relative to this file's own directory. Declaring it is what turns recording on: with no audit member this runtime writes nothing at all, and with one, every evaluation the CLI's experimental evaluate and the MCP experimental_evaluate tool complete appends one record, and every experimental graph evaluate one per node and one for the composite. Test runs — packs test, experimental graph test, experimental evaluate-corpus — never record: a run of a matrix is not a decision anyone took. A run declared a rehearsal (the CLI's --rehearsal on either command, the tool's rehearsal argument) never records either (ADR-0028, ADR-0041). The trail is chained unless chain is false (ADR-0047). Declaring it requires configVersion "3".

configVersion.description: The version of this configuration format. A single integer as a string, on the outputVersion precedent rather than semantic versioning. "1" is the shape without graphs, "2" the shape with them, "3" the shape that may also ask for an audit trail, "4" the shape that may also require its deciding runs to apply its reviewed set, "5" the shape that may also require every fact a comparison reads to be of a type that comparison can match, and "6" the shape whose audit member may also say whether its trail is chained; this runtime reads all six, and this schema accepts no other, so a configuration held to these exact bytes is held to what the runtime will actually read. A runtime that knows only the earlier shapes refuses a later configuration as unsupported while naming what it accepts, which is the actionable path the version gate exists to give — an unknown member under an earlier version would be an invalid-config refusal that takes every project surface down with it.

graphs.description: EXPERIMENTAL graphs composing this project's packs (ADR-0015, ADR-0017), keyed by the project's own name for one graph — the graph document's id member is the graph's identity and is not this key, exactly as a pack entry's key is not the pack's id. Declaring any graph requires configVersion "2" or later. The graph surface may change or be removed without compatibility promise, and a project that declares no graph never needs this member or that version.

packs.description: The project's packs, keyed by decision id. The key is the project's own name for one decision; the pack document's id member is the pack's identity and is not this key. A newly created project may have no packs yet. A test run over zero rows is skipped, never passed.

requireComparableFacts.description: Whether an evaluation must refuse a fact no comparison that reads it can match (ADR-0046). There is no coercion between JSON types, so a fact of another type than every operand of an equals, not-equals or in -- null included -- makes equals and in false and not-equals true, never unknown, and onUnknown does not reach it; an ordered comparison reads a decimal string and nothing else, so a string outside the decimal grammar matches it no more than a JSON number does. When true, the CLI's experimental evaluate and experimental graph evaluate, for every node, and the MCP experimental_evaluate tool refuse (JPS-FACTS-COMPARABLE-REQUIRED), after the inputs are admitted and before anything is evaluated, every evaluation in which a fact that some comparison anywhere in the pack reads is present and of a type that comparison can never match, whether or not evaluation would reach that comparison. The check's work is bounded by the evaluation's work limit, and a check that would pass it refuses under the same code, whatever the pack compares. The refusal is the project's, not an evaluation error, and carries no JPS §8.4 class. A fact that is absent is not refused: it is unknown, and the pack's onUnknown governs it. Declared rehearsals are refused too, since a rehearsal's answer is read as well. The test surfaces are not -- packs test, experimental graph test, experimental evaluate-corpus, experimental compare and the MCP test tools -- because their rows and inputs may probe such facts on purpose. Absent or false, such a fact is evaluated as Core says. Declaring it requires configVersion "5".

requireReviewed.description: Whether every deciding run must apply this project's reviewed set (ADR-0044). When true, the CLI's experimental evaluate and experimental graph evaluate and the MCP experimental_evaluate tool refuse, before any evaluation, a run that applies a draft (a pack named by path or passed as text, or a graph document this configuration does not declare) and every run when the project has declared no reviewed set (ADR-0019). A declared rehearsal is not a decision and is not refused. The member binds only a caller who neither chooses which configuration a run reads nor can edit this file or the project's reviewed set: whoever chooses the configuration chooses whether it applies, whoever can edit these files can turn it off, and an edit to this file is itself an amendment the reviewed set records. Absent or false, drafts are evaluated and recorded as drafts, as before. Declaring it requires configVersion "4" or later.

dir.description: The directory the records are appended to. It is a directory rather than a file, and the constraints differ from a declared file's accordingly: it need not exist — the first record creates it — a symlink to a directory inside this file's own directory is followed like any other component, and a symlink pointing out of it is the escape packs validate reports as the audit-dir-inside-root check and the write refuses again. Nothing outside can be created, named, or written, whatever the pathname would suggest. One file is written in it, evaluations.jsonl, one JSON record per line. On unix that file is kept owner-readable only; on Windows a file mode sets only the read-only attribute and does not restrict the DACL, so what may read a record there is whatever the directory's ACL allows. The directory's own mode is set when this runtime creates it and never afterward: a directory the project made is the project's, and its access control stays the project's.

chain.description: Whether the trail is chained (ADR-0047). Absent or true, each record this runtime appends also carries trail (the trail's identity, 128 random bits in hex), sequence (its line number in the file, from 1) and previous (the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of the line before it, without its newline; for a chained record that follows no chained line, of the whole file before it, which commits to every earlier line at once and rewrites none of them). The writer holds the file exclusively against every other writer that cooperates while it reads the last line, assigns the sequences, writes, and syncs the file and its directory; it refuses to append after an incomplete last line, when a line it must read or would write is longer than 128 MiB, and when other writers cannot be excluded for a reason that may pass, and only where the platform or file system cannot exclude other writers at all does it append the record unchained. False appends records without those members, without excluding other writers and without reading the file, as runtimes before configVersion "6" did. The links show whether the lines are consistent with one another, not that the history is authentic: an edit to any line but the last breaks a link, but the last line can be edited, and a trail cut short or rewritten from any line on with its links recomputed, without breaking one; only a commitment held by someone other than the operator, covering those lines, tells them apart. jpack audit verify checks the links, and jpack audit checkpoint prints such a commitment for handing over. Declaring it requires configVersion "6".

relativeFilePath.description: A relative path naming one file. Containment is the relativePath rule and nothing here relaxes it; on top of it, a final component that is a symlink is refused whatever it points at, and only a regular file is read.

relativePath.description: A path relative to this configuration file's own directory, which it must resolve inside. Two different checks say so and neither substitutes for the other: a lexical check refuses an absolute or escaping path before anything is opened, and at access time the path is resolved against a handle held open on that directory -- which is what catches a path reaching outside through a symlinked component, since a lexical check cannot see one, and what keeps containment true through the open rather than only up to it. What the final component may be depends on what the member names, and each member says so: this is the containment rule and nothing more.

path.description: The pack document, relative to this file's directory.

matrix.description: The pack's instance matrix, relative to this file's directory. Rows carry the fields the evaluation comparator reads, shared with the bundled evaluation corpus, plus this convention's own expectedHandoffTarget under matrixVersion 2; the corpus separately requires members a project row need not declare, so the two are judged alike rather than interchangeable.

description.description: One line about the decision this pack encodes, for a human or an agent reading the inventory.

expectedVersion.description: The pack document version this project expects. It is a validated reference and never an independent truth: packs validate reports a difference from the document's own version member as an error rather than preferring either value.

facts.description: NON-NORMATIVE agent hints, keyed by the RFC 6901 JSON Pointer the pack's conditions read. They say where a fact is found; they are not facts, and this runtime never reads a source. The key is checked against the pack document by packs validate: a pointer no condition reads is reported as a failed check rather than handed to an agent as an instruction.

evidence.description: NON-NORMATIVE agent hints, keyed by the pack's declared evidence-requirement ids. They say where evidence is found; they are not evidence, and this runtime never reads a source. The key is checked against the pack document by packs validate: an id the pack declares no requirement for is reported as a failed check.

path.description: The graph document, relative to this file's directory.

rows.description: The graph's matrix, relative to this file's directory: rows run by experimental graph test. Optional — a graph without rows validates in the project walk and is skipped by the test walk, which says so.

description.description: One line about the composition this graph declares, for a human or an agent reading the inventory.

source.description: Where the value is authoritatively held, in the project's own words -- a warehouse table, a document library, a service. The runtime holds no credential and opens no connection; reading it is the agent's job, with the agent's own access.

hint.description: How to obtain the value from that source, in the project's own words.
